status: declared before any v2 fit or score; owner (20 Nov): 'Continue this one' after plan.json failed (reports/HERDERS_20261120.md)
question: Does a herding share built on crop marginality (short growing season or low plant growth) with a humid-tropics livestock penalty rank where societies herd, on societies never used before?
development: all 546 Ethnographic Atlas societies of plan.json (0-56 N, 12 W - 125 E; all seen)
blind: Ethnographic Atlas societies in Africa and Madagascar south of the equator (36 S - 0, 8 - 52 E) with both EA004 and EA005: 145 (9 mainly herders); the Earth run is rebuilt on that window with land_people_earth.py --window (same code)
target: observed herding share EA004 / (EA004 + EA005) at bin midpoints; mainly herders = EA004 bin > EA005 bin (as plan.json)

rule.form: H = b + a x M x (1 - p x W); M = marginality ramp, W = humid-hot indicator (growing season > Lw days and annual mean T > 20 C)
rule.level: b, a by least squares on development (a >= 0, H clipped to 0-1); all fields from the Earth run at the 15-arc-min mean, as plan.json
rule.choice: the single (family, ramp, Lw, p) with the highest development Spearman; ties -> lower squared error

blind_gates.G2: v2 blind Spearman >= current model's blind Spearman + 0.15
blind_gates.reported_only: blind mainly-herders balanced accuracy at H > 0.5 (9 positives: too few to gate), mean levels
blind_gates.adopt: G1 and G2: H becomes the map's herding share (a new 'Herders and farmers' layer and the per-polity herding statistics). Grazing capacity, food capacity and population stay unchanged (a separate question). Otherwise the share stays and the result is reported.
